raw_case_text:
A 42-year-old female, homemaker presented with complaints of swelling in both inguinal region for 6 months. Swelling developed initially on the left and then on the right side. Both the swellings ruptured spontaneously one after the other in the order of their appearance, discharging serous material, associated with dull aching pain. Not associated with any genital ulcer, vaginal discharge, and lower abdominal pain. There was no history of fever, weight loss, and cough with expectoration. She is a married woman with no premarital or extramarital contact history.
On examination, the patient was thin built with no signs of anemia, icterus, cyanosis or clubbing. She had bilateral palpable matted lymph nodes in the inguinal region. The one on the right side measured about 8 cm x 4 cm, oval in shape, with well-defined margins and irregular surface. On the left side the swelling was minimal with ill-defined margins and discharging sinus [Figure 1]. Skin over both the inguinal nodes showed healed scars. Examination of the external genitalia revealed no specific finding. Systemic examination did not reveal any abnormality.
Investigations showed hemoglobin 10.6 g%, total leukocyte count 7600/cmm, neutrophil 63%, lymphocyte 30%, eosinophil 4%. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 36 mm/h. Serum total protein, albumin and globulin ratio were within normal limits. Urine routine was normal. Chest X-ray, ultrasonography abdomen and pelvis, PAP smear were not contributory. Serological screening for retroviral status and syphilis were non-reactive. Mantoux test was highly positive showing induration of 25 mm (+++) [Figure 2]. Fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of the lymph node showed presence of Langhans giant cells, epithelioid cells and lymphocytes suggestive of tuberculous lymphadenitis. She was not willing for lymph node biopsy. Category I anti-tubercular treatment comprised of 2 months intensive phase with isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol and 4 months continuation phase with isoniazid and rifampicin was instituted. Patient was followed-up periodically, and there was complete resolution by the end of treatment [Figure 3].

subjective.chief_complaint: A 42-year-old female presented with a 6-month history of bilateral inguinal swelling that ruptured with serous discharge and dull aching pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 42-year-old female noticed a swelling in the left inguinal region that was followed by a similar swelling on the right side over a 6-month period. Both swellings subsequently ruptured spontaneously in the sequence of their appearance, draining serous material with associated dull aching pain. She denied genital ulcers, vaginal discharge, lower abdominal pain, fever, weight loss, or chronic cough.
subjective.past_medical_history: Married woman with no premarital or extramarital contact history. No other prior medical conditions, hospitalizations, or antibiotic exposures documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for dull aching inguinal pain and serous discharge. Negative for genital ulceration, vaginal discharge, lower abdominal pain, fever, weight loss, or cough with expectoration. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Thin built, no anemia, jaundice, cyanosis, or clubbing. Bilateral palpable matted inguinal lymph nodes: right-sided mass 8 cm x 4 cm, oval, well-defined, irregular surface; left side minimal swelling with ill-defined margins and discharging sinus. Overlying skin exhibited healed scars. External genitalia and systemic examinations normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 10.6 g%, total leukocyte count 7600/cmm (neutrophils 63%, lymphocytes 30%, eosinophils 4%), ESR 36 mm/h. Serum total protein, albumin, and globulin ratio normal. Routine urinalysis normal. Chest radiograph, abdominal/pelvic ultrasound, and Pap smear non-contributory. Screening for HIV and syphilis non-reactive. Mantoux test strongly positive with 25 mm induration (+++).
objective.advanced_workup: Fine needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of inguinal lymph node: presence of Langhans giant cells, epithelioid cells, and lymphocytes suggestive of granulomatous lymphadenitis. Patient declined excisional lymph node biopsy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Tuberculous inguinal lymphadenitis with spontaneous sinus tract formation, confirmed by lymph node fine needle aspiration cytology showing Langhans giant cells, epithelioid cells, and granulomatous inflammation, accompanied by a strongly positive Mantoux test (25 mm induration). Sexually transmitted infections (syphilis, HIV) were ruled out. Management & Outcome: Treated with Category I antitubercular regimen: 2-month intensive phase of isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol, followed by 4-month continuation phase of isoniazid and rifampicin. Demonstrated complete resolution of lymphadenopathy and healed sinus tracts at conclusion of therapy.
